title: Semantic conventions: names everyone agrees on
summary: Why attribute and span names are standardised, what is stable at the end of 2026 (HTTP, database, RPC) and what is not (messaging), and how to name spans and migrate old attributes.

steps.title: Same names, every language, every vendor
body: The **semantic conventions** (semconv) name the attributes, span names and metrics for common operations, so a dashboard or an alert
works whatever library or language produced the data. They are versioned (v1.45.0 came out on 2 November 2026) and every part has

| Database client spans and metrics | **stable** (core attributes; per-database pages vary) | `db.system.name`, `db.namespace`, `db.collection.name`, `db.operation.name`, `db.query.text`, `db.query.summary` |
| RPC (gRPC, Dubbo) | **stable since 1.45** | `rpc.system`, `rpc.method`, call duration metrics |
Older instrumentation still emits the pre-stable names (`http.method`, `http.status_code`, `db.statement`, `db.system`). Most
instrumentations let you migrate with `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` (`http/dup` or `database/dup` emit both while dashboards move).
The .NET ASP.NET Core and HttpClient instrumentation and Npgsql 10 already emit the stable names: the lab's spans show
`db.query.text` and `db.system.name`. For messaging, pin your library version and expect renames.

steps.prompt: Match the old (pre-stable) attribute to its stable name.
What should the **server** span of `GET /api/products/17` be named?
steps.explain: Span names must be low-cardinality: `{method} {route}`. The raw path makes a new name per product, so the backend's operation list, its latency stats and any span-name metric blow up. The concrete path goes in `url.path`. Without a route (a 404 that matched nothing) the name is just the method.

steps.prompt: Stable, or still in development, as of semconv 1.45 (November 2026)?
steps.explain: Build alerts and long-lived dashboards on stable names. Development names can still be renamed in a minor release, as `messaging.system` just was.

steps.title: Name spans by the conventions
prompt: **`string HttpSpanName(string method, string? route)`**: `"{METHOD} {route}"`, or just `"{METHOD}"` when the route is null or
empty. The method is upper-cased; if it is not one of `GET HEAD POST PUT DELETE CONNECT OPTIONS TRACE PATCH`, use `HTTP` instead
(the conventions' rule for unknown methods, so a scanner sending `FOOBAR` cannot create new span names).
**`string DbSpanName(string? summary, string? operation, string? collection, string? ns, string system)`**, in this order:
2. else `"{operation} {target}"` when there is an operation and a target, where target is `collection`, else `ns`;
3. else the target alone (or the operation alone when there is no target);
starter: string HttpSpanName(string method, string? route) => method;
string DbSpanName(string? summary, string? operation, string? collection, string? ns, string system) => system;
solution: string DbSpanName(string? summary, string? operation, string? collection, string? ns, string system)
static string? Val(string? s) => string.IsNullOrEmpty(s) ? null : s;
if (op is not null && target is not null) return $"{op} {target}";
hints: For the database: `var target = Val(collection) ?? Val(ns);` then the three cases in order.
template: Dojo.Eq("unknown method with a route", "HTTP /api/checkout", HttpSpanName("PROPFIND", "/api/checkout"));
Dojo.Eq("a summary wins", "SELECT reviews", DbSpanName("SELECT reviews", "SELECT", "reviews", "shop", "postgresql"));
Dojo.Eq("operation and namespace", "SELECT shop", DbSpanName("", "SELECT", null, "shop", "postgresql"));
Dojo.Eq("nothing but the system (what Npgsql names its spans)", "postgresql", DbSpanName(null, null, null, null, "postgresql"));

steps.title: Migrate old attributes
prompt: A legacy service still sends pre-stable names and the platform team rewrites them in the Collector. Write the rule as C#:
`Dictionary<string, object> Upgrade(Dictionary<string, object> attrs)` returns a **new** dictionary where
- every other key is kept as it is;
- if both the old and the new name are present, the **new** value wins and the old key is dropped.
Values keep their type (an `int` status code stays an `int`).
solution: if (renames.TryGetValue(k, out var stable)) { if (!attrs.ContainsKey(stable)) result[stable] = v; }
hints: A rename map, then one loop: an old key is written under its new name unless the new name is already in the input.
Do not modify the input dictionary: build a new one.
template: Dojo.Check("the status code stays an int", dojoNew.GetValueOrDefault("http.response.status_code") is int dojoCode && dojoCode == 200, "");
Dojo.Check("the input still has the old key", dojoOld.ContainsKey("http.method"), "");
Dojo.Eq("the stable value wins", "SELECT 1", dojoBoth.GetValueOrDefault("db.query.text") as string);
Dojo.Eq("no old keys left", "db.query.text,db.system.name", string.Join(",", dojoBoth.Keys.Order()));
